title: #60 Student Grouping
prompt: Some people think schools should group students according to their academic abilities while others think students can achieve better performance in mixed groups. Discuss both opinions and give your own opinion.

angles.label: Point 1
angles.en: Grouping students by ability helps students learn better because they work with similar skills.

angles.label: Point 2
angles.en: Mixed groups are good for all students because they allow students to learn from different abilities.

angles.label: Point 2

angles.label: Point 1
angles.en: The essay argues that grouping students by ability is better because it allows for focused learning and helps students reach their full potential.
angles.vi: Góc nhìn: The essay argues that grouping students by ability is better because it allows for focused learning and helps students reach their full potential.

angles.label: Point 2
angles.en: The essay acknowledges that mixed groups are beneficial because students can learn from their peers, but maintains that ability grouping is superior.

angles.label: Point 1
angles.en: The essay discusses the view that grouping students by ability is beneficial, using the structure: Point (Grouping by ability) -> Explain (Similar skills) -> Example (Math/reading class) -> Effect (Focused teaching) -> Link (Learn at own pace).
angles.vi: Góc nhìn: The essay discusses the view that grouping students by ability is beneficial, using the structure: Point (Grouping by ability) -> Explain (Similar skills) -> Example (Math/reading class) -> Effect (Focused teaching) -> Link (Learn at own pace).

angles.label: Point 2
angles.en: The essay discusses the view that mixed groups are better, using the structure: Point (Mixed groups are better) -> Explain (Learn from classmates) -> Example (Writing help) -> Effect (Develop skills in many ways) -> Link (Richer learning experience).

modelPlan.focus: Discuss both opinions on whether schools should group students by academic ability or use mixed groups, and present my own opinion.
outline: Arguments for grouping by academic ability
Arguments against grouping by academic ability
keyArguments: Grouping by ability can provide targeted instruction and support, potentially improving academic outcomes.
Mixed groups promote inclusivity and social skills, but may hinder individual progress due to varying learning paces.
